issues.legal_issue: An allottee who accepts the allotment terms, pays an extension fee to obtain an extension and avoid resumption, and receives that benefit cannot later seek a refund by repudiating the liability he accepted.
material_facts: The allotment required construction within a specified period and was subject to the governing enactment, rules, and allotment conditions.
After construction was not completed, the authority demanded an extension fee and warned that the plot could be resumed if payment was not made.
The allottee agreed to pay and paid the fee to avoid resumption, thereby obtaining the benefit of an extension.
After receiving that benefit, the allottee sought a refund on the basis of a later rule and a prior decision concerning extension fees.
The High Court directed recalculation and refund, and the authority appealed that order.
issues.conclusion: The allottee could not accept and benefit from the extension arrangement and later deny the corresponding liability. The prior decision relied on by the High Court did not govern these materially different facts. The appeals were allowed and the High Court's order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The doctrine of approbate and reprobate is a species of estoppel based on election: a person who knowingly accepts the benefit of an order or transaction cannot later deny its binding effect to obtain a different advantage. Estoppel cannot operate against a statute. The Court relied on C.I.T. v. Mr. P. Firm Maur, AIR 1965 SC 1216; Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation v. Balwant Regular Motor Service, AIR 1969 SC 329; R.N. Gosain v. Yashpal Dhir, AIR 1993 SC 352; Sri Babu Ram Alias Durga Prasad v. Sri Indra Pal Singh, AIR 1998 SC 3021; P.R. Deshpande v. Maruti Balram Haibatti, AIR 1998 SC 2979; and Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation v. Diamond and Gem Development Corporation, AIR 2013 SC 1241. The Court distinguished Tehal Singh v. State of Punjab, which concerned demands for extension fees under Rule 13 of the Punjab Regional and Town Planning and Development (General) Rules, 1995, because the allottee here had accepted and acted on the allotment terms and received the extension benefit.

rule.if: appeal_against_refund_order and allotment_terms_accepted and extension_fee_paid and extension_benefit_received and refund_claim_made_afterwards

predicates.appeal_against_refund_order: An authority appeals an order directing it to recalculate or refund a fee paid by an allottee.
predicates.allotment_terms_accepted: The allottee accepts terms that govern the allotment and the consequences of failing to meet its requirements.
predicates.extension_fee_paid: After the authority demands a fee for extending the time to comply with an allotment requirement, the allottee pays that fee.
predicates.extension_benefit_received: The allottee receives the extension or other benefit for which the demanded fee was paid.
predicates.refund_claim_made_afterwards: After receiving the benefit, the allottee seeks to recover the fee by disputing the liability he previously accepted.

issues.definition: When an allottee accepts the governing terms, pays a demanded fee, receives the benefit for that payment, and later seeks a refund while the refund order is under appeal, the refund claim is barred by election.
